segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus gathered his closest friends around one table in an upper room, knowing the night would change everything.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I have wanted this meal with you, he told them — wanted it badly — before the hard thing happens. He knew what was coming that night, and what he wanted first was to sit down and eat with his friends.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This is my body, he said, and it is given for you. Do this to remember me. Not a symbol he was explaining — a gift he was handing over, piece by piece, into their hands.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After the meal he lifted the cup, and gave it to them, too.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This cup is the new covenant in my blood, he said — poured out for you. A brand new promise between God and people, and he was signing it with his own life.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said he would not drink the fruit of the vine again until the kingdom of God arrives. He was telling them this was not goodbye — it was see you at the next meal. Then he and his friends sang together and walked out into the night.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The bread and the cup, still on the table — a gift to remember him by.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He left a simple meal to remember him by. Come to his table — he is still the host.
